bugHunt.title: Bug Hunt
bugHunt.description: Read short programs and spot the faulty line. Your longest correct-answer streak is tracked separately.
bugHunt.instructions: Inspect ten snippets. From stage two, choose a fix; from stage six, enter the corrected output too. Each stage earns 100 points.
bugHunt.selectFix: Now choose the correct replacement for that line.
bugHunt.selectOutput: What does the corrected code print?
bugHunt.outputHint: Separate list items with commas, for example [1, 2, 3].
bugHunt.ruleText: Find the faulty line. From stage two, choose its repair. From stage six, enter what the repaired code prints.
bugHunt.pointsHint: Earn 100 points only when every answer in the stage is correct

sum.task: The sum should be 10, but it prints 5.
sum.explain: The loop replaces the total each time. Add the number to the total instead.

range.task: Print the sequence 2, 5, 8, 11, including its final value.
range.explain: range excludes stop. Increase the stop by one to include 11 without changing the step.

average.task: Find the weighted average of the three marks. It should be 7.5.
average.explain: The weighted sum must be divided by the total weight, not the number of marks.

maximum.task: Print the first index of the largest value. Both 9s tie, so the answer is 1.
maximum.explain: Updating on equality replaces the first maximum with the later one. Update only for a strictly larger value.

even.task: Only even numbers should remain: 2 and 4.
even.explain: An even number has a remainder of 0 when divided by 2.

reverse.task: Reverse the six values in place with two pointers.
reverse.explain: Each swap moves both pointers one step inward. Moving right by two skips a required swap.

contains.task: For every target, check whether a name matches, ignoring letter case.
contains.explain: some must find an equal normalized name. A different name does not prove a target is present.

factorial.task: Calculate the factorials of 3, 4 and 5 in one loop.
factorial.explain: The inner loop must multiply by its changing value, not repeat the outer number.

search.task: Find the first index of a, even though it appears twice. Print 1.
search.explain: After the first match, keep its index instead of overwriting it with a later match.

count.task: Three words start with s, so the count should be 3.
count.explain: Increase the count when a word matches; this line decreases it.

slice.task: Starting at index 1, take three numbers: 20, 30 and 40.
slice.explain: slice takes an end index, not a count. Add count to start to find the exclusive end.

positive.task: Only 3 and 5 should count as positive.
positive.explain: Zero is not positive. Use > 0 instead of >= 0.

any_all.task: For each class, check whether at least one score is below 50.
any_all.explain: Use some inside map. Every asks whether all scores in that class are below 50.

palindrome.task: Check each word for a palindrome and print the four results.
palindrome.explain: At index zero, -index points to the first character. Use -index - 1 for the mirrored character.

sort.task: Sort by priority, then time, then ID, all ascending.
sort.explain: The time comparison runs backward. Keep the priority and ID comparisons, and compare a.time - b.time.

prefix.task: Use prefix sums to answer the three half-open ranges [left, right).
prefix.explain: For a half-open range, subtract prefix[left] from prefix[right]. Adding one to left skips its first value.

unique.task: Trim spaces and remove repeated names without regard to case, keeping the first spelling.
unique.explain: The check uses the lowercase key, so seen must store that same key rather than the original spelling.

frequency.task: Count paid orders by city, trimming spaces and ignoring case. Skip pending orders.
frequency.explain: Read the existing count with the normalized city. Looking up the original spelling resets several groups.

window.task: Find the largest three-number sum and the first starting index that achieves it.
window.explain: When the window moves right, remove the value at right - width. The extra one corrupts both the sum and its first index.

lower_bound.task: For targets 7, 8 and 20, return each first index whose value is at least the target.
lower_bound.explain: An equal value may be the first valid result. Move left only when values[mid] < target, including the duplicate 8s.

logicCircuit.title: Logic Circuit
logicCircuit.description: Wire gates to match the target truth table. Fewer checks mean more points.
logicCircuit.task: Choose the gates and optional NOT stage so your output matches every target row.
logicCircuit.secondGate: Second gate · first result and C
logicCircuit.tableHint: Your output appears after the first check.
logicCircuit.tryAgain: {{count}} of {{total}} rows match. Change a gate and check again.
logicCircuit.doneDetail: You built all ten circuits. Try again to solve them in fewer checks.

and.title: Both switches
and.hint: The light turns on only when both inputs are on.

xor.title: Exactly one
xor.hint: The light turns on when exactly one input is on.

xnor.title: Matching switches
xnor.hint: The light is on when both inputs have the same state: both off or both on.

switch.title: Difference signal
switch.hint: Compare C with the signal made when A and B are both on. The output lights when those signals differ.

gate.title: Blocked signal
gate.hint: The output lights only when A and B are both on while C is off.

filter.title: Counter-signal
filter.hint: C must be off; then either A or B can activate the output.

splitChannels.title: Split channels
splitChannels.hint: Compare the A–B AND signal with the C–D parity signal; the output lights when they differ.

evenParity.title: Balance
evenParity.hint: Compare rows with an even and odd number of active inputs. The same operation may work for both pairs.

mixed.title: Crossed signals
mixed.hint: Split the 16 rows into groups of four. Look for a smaller pattern that repeats when the right inputs are paired.

final.title: Final checkpoint
final.hint: Compare A–D parity with the B–C AND signal. Check whether the final output needs inverting.

memoryGrid.title: Memory Grid
memoryGrid.description: Watch a sequence of cells and tap it back in order. The sequence speeds up as the grid expands.
memoryGrid.instructions: Tap the lit cells in order. Ten rounds, two lives. Mistakes cost no points; replay costs 25.
memoryGrid.doneDetail: {{cleared}} of {{total}} rounds cleared. Try again to improve your score.
memoryGrid.watchHint: Wait until the final cell fades before tapping.
memoryGrid.inputHint: Tap the highlighted cells in the same order.
memoryGrid.mistake: That was a different cell. One life was used; watch the pattern again.
